Symbol-inside-montage nesting is explicitly SUPPORTED, montage-inside-symbol is explicitly REFUSED — confirmed by reading all four entry guards together, not assumed from either function's own comment in isolation. enterSymbol's own guard (app.js:4152-4154) checks ONLY `state.activeSymbolId`, never `state.activeMontageViewId` — so double-clicking a montage-view segment (itself a real `symbolId` layer, per enterMontageView's own header comment 4268-4270) while inside a montage view correctly swaps into `_sceneSnapshot` a SECOND time, capturing the montage view's own synthetic `state.layers` (the `newLayers` array built at 4326-4340) as the thing exitToScene will later restore — exactly the 'treats the montage view's synthetic layers as the scene to snapshot/restore' design the comment names. No corresponding guard exists (or is needed) forcing exit of a montage view before entering a DIFFERENT montage view from inside a symbol, because entering a symbol never sets `state.activeMontageViewId` and montage views are never entered from inside a symbol's own UI surface.

Every Paper.js side effect in this scope, with lines, and the ASYMMETRY between the two view-switch pairs' own Paper-layer lifecycle: enterSymbol calls `ensureSymbolPaperLayers(symId)` (4182, C21l territory, cited by line) — a MEMOIZED cache keyed by symId (declared in C21k, populated in C21l) that creates each sub-layer's real `paper.Layer` exactly ONCE ever and simply flips `.visible`/`.opacity` on repeat entries (4183); exitToScene mirrors this by only flipping `.visible=false` (4242), never removing. enterMontageView, by contrast, has NO cache at all: it calls `arcLayer.activate()` (4321, Paper.js context activation before constructing new Layers — enterSymbol never calls this directly since ensureSymbolPaperLayers does its own activate() internally, C21l-territory) then constructs a BRAND-NEW `new Layer({name:'montageview-'+montageId+'-'+newUls.length})` (4341) for every chain member on every single call, `.insertBelow(arcLayer)`+`.visible=true` (4348, the actual project-layer-stack insertion — the Layers are constructed but not yet attached/visible until this line) — and exitMontageView unconditionally `.remove()`s every one of them (4362), so a montage view's own Paper layers are a fresh construct/destroy pair every single enter/exit cycle, never cached. propagateLFSFill has its own THIRD, throwaway-scoped Paper.js lifecycle: `new Layer({name:'lfs-propagate-scratch'})` (4116, immediately hidden), `.removeChildren()` once per target frame inside the tfi loop to reuse the same scratch layer (4126), and a final `.remove()` (4146) once the whole function is done — confirmed via direct read, no external caller ever sees this layer.
